newsitem.title: DUBAI: British trade minister Anthony Nelson leaves Oman.
newsitem.headline: British trade minister Anthony Nelson leaves Oman.

text.p: British trade minister Anthony Nelson left Oman on Tuesday after a five-day visit in which he met key Omani officials, a British embassy spokesman said.
The spokesman said the aim of the visit had been "to reinforce the UK's commercial commitment in its relations with Oman and to find out how Oman's privatisation is progressing".
Oman, like other Gulf Arab states, is trying to diversify its oil-driven economy and encourage the private sector.
Nelson's delegation included 15 bankers and businessmen.
"Most were considering becoming involved in the projects planned in next five years," the embassy official said in reference to a string of planned infrastructure projects.
Nelson met Oman's ministers of commerce and industry, water, the minister of state for development affairs, the head of the Muscat Securities Market and other senior officials.
The embassy spokesman said Nelson stressed that British companies "needed to have a clear idea how things were expected to progress and know what Oman's priorities were".
Britain exported goods worth about 450 million pounds ($711 million) to Oman in 1995, while about 70 million pounds worth of goods went the other way, he said.
